title: Quiz: Introduction to Rates of Reaction

questions.stem: What is the correct definition of rate of reaction?

options.text: The total amount of product formed in a reaction
How fast reactants are converted into products
The energy needed to start a reaction
The temperature at which a reaction occurs

questions.explanation: Rate of reaction measures how fast reactants are converted into products, expressed as the amount of reactant used or product formed per unit time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct unit for rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: Rate of reaction is measured as amount per unit time. cm³/s (volume of gas per second) is a valid unit, along with g/s and mol/s.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a fast reaction?

options.text: Neutralisation of an acid with an alkali

questions.explanation: Acid-alkali neutralisation is a fast reaction that happens almost instantaneously, whereas rusting, fermentation, and rock weathering are slow reactions that take much longer.

questions.stem: On a graph of volume of gas produced against time, what does the gradient (slope) of the curve represent?

options.text: The total volume of gas produced
The rate of reaction at that point

questions.explanation: The gradient of a graph of product formed against time equals the rate of reaction at that point. A steeper gradient means a faster rate.

questions.stem: During a typical reaction, when is the rate of reaction fastest?

options.text: At the start of the reaction
At the end of the reaction

questions.explanation: The rate is fastest at the start because the concentration of reactant particles is highest, leading to the most frequent collisions. As reactants are used up, the rate decreases.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a factor that affects the rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: The colour of reactants does not affect the rate of reaction. The main factors are concentration, temperature, surface area, presence of a catalyst, and pressure (for gases).

questions.stem: If 60 cm³ of gas is produced in 30 seconds, what is the average rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: Rate = amount of product / time = 60 cm³ / 30 s = 2.0 cm³/s.
